new_statements.rule_in_words: The only first-hand prosodic remark covering Barikewa: tone (pitch) carries a grammatical contrast (affirmative vs negative verb) in Barikewa as in Ikobi and Mouwase; the survey wordlists record Barikewa forms with syllable-by-syllable pitch diacritics. No statement of where word stress falls, whether stress exists, or how lexical tone works.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the illustrating examples are Ikobi (Moka village), the claim is asserted for Barikewa by extension.
new_statements.domain_note: Sociolinguistic survey, not a phonology; the remark concerns grammatical tone on verbs. Usher (NewGuineaWorld, comparative) adds second-hand that tone is contrastive in the Omati River group and that there is no published phonology of Barikewa.
new_statements.identity_note: Bullock 2015's Barikewa data come from Kaiam village (Kaiam 1 list) and from two Barikewa ('Iba') speakers resident in mixed Omati village (list elicited by R. Petterson); 76% lexical similarity between the two. Barikewa = Glottolog bari1298 / ISO jbk, split from retired Omati [mgx] in 2012; Franklin's 1973 'Omati (Mini)' corresponds mainly to Mouwase [jmw] (mouw1234), and his 'Barika' (AR 1921-22, Asanu) to Barikewa. The tonal-negation examples quoted are from Ikobi [meb] (ikob1240), Moka village, with the claim extended to Barikewa.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Appendix A p.34: 'in all three languages [Ikobi, Mouwase, Barikewa], negation can be indicated tonally' (Ikobi examples). Appendix C Table 19 (pp.57-61): two Barikewa 190-item wordlists (Omati/Iba by Petterson, Kaiam 1 by Spencer) in IPA with pitch diacritics on vowels; no prosodic analysis.

sources.note: Proto-Omati River historical phonology: 'Tone is contrastive, but has not been indicated in the protoforms'. Barikewa forms (Petterson 1991, Carr 2006) cited with tone diacritics, Kaser/Mowase (Carr) with stress marks; no synchronic stress rule for Barikewa. Kaser page (after Petterson 2011 unpublished phonology) silent on stress/tone.
